articles.title_original: Israeli forces begin demolishing Palestinian buildings in Hebron after two Israeli soldiers shot dead
articles.title_zh: Israeli forces begin demolishing Palestinian buildings in Hebron after two Israeli soldiers shot dead
facts_zh:
Israeli forces begin demolishing Palestinian buildings in Hebron after two Israeli soldiers shot dead
- Published
The Israeli military has begun demolishing Palestinian buildings in the city of Hebron, after two Israeli soldiers were killed in an attack by two Palestinian gunmen.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the military would "destroy" the neighbourhood where the two attackers came from, and that Israel was ready for "extensive action" in the occupied West Bank.
Three other soldiers were wounded in the attack at a checkpoint outside Hebron, before the gunmen were shot dead, officials say.

all_titles.en: Israeli forces begin demolishing Palestinian buildings in Hebron after two Israeli soldiers shot dead

articles.title_original: Oil spill washes up on UAE beaches after tanker strike
articles.title_zh: Oil spill washes up on UAE beaches after tanker strike
facts_zh:
Oil spill washes up on UAE beaches after tanker strike
- Published
An oil spill from a tanker attacked near the Strait of Hormuz is spreading along the United Arab Emirates (UAE) coastline, forcing the closure of some beaches and coastal areas.

Satellite images from Monday show the beginnings of the oil spill from a ship matching the location and dimensions of Gem No.2, which was damaged between 9 and 10 October during a record surge of vessel strikes by Iran.
The slick of oil had spread more than 35km (22 miles) from the tanker by Wednesday, the satellite imagery showed.

all_titles.en: Oil spill washes up on UAE beaches after tanker strike

articles.title_original: Denmark to ban mink farming in government U-turn
articles.title_zh: Denmark to ban mink farming in government U-turn
facts_zh:
Denmark to ban mink farming in government U-turn
- Published
Mink farming will end in Denmark by August 2029 after the government decided to drop plans to pursue an exemption to an EU-wide ban on the practice.

Denmark was once the largest producer of mink fur in the world, but the industry has declined due to global bans on fur farming, a decline in the fur trade and an earlier outbreak of a Covid strain in the nation's mink population.
The ban is due to come into effect on 7 August next year, and is followed by a two-year transition period to phase out the practice.

all_titles.en: Denmark to ban mink farming in government U-turn

articles.title_zh: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
facts_zh:
Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
- Published
Ukraine is still recording issues with the Starlink network, sources within the defence ministry say, after Donald Trump said limits on the satellite uplink had been reversed by Elon Musk.
The sources told the BBC that instances of drones experiencing connection loss at speeds of 161km/h (100mph) were being recorded, hampering military operations.
The US president had denied instructing the tech billionaire to restrict connectivity to Starlink's military-grade counterpart, Starshield, before saying on Thursday that Musk had "put it back".

all_titles.en: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted

facts_zh:
Cyprus police open investigation into financial affairs of Roman Abramovich
- Published
Police in Cyprus have opened an investigation into the financial affairs of Roman Abramovich, following revelations by BBC Panorama that accountancy firm Deloitte helped in falsifying documents to hide his wealth and evade tax.
Serious questions about the integrity of some of Abramovich's professional advisers were raised earlier this month in a joint report from the BBC and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism (TBIJ).
A Cypriot Ministry of Justice official told MPs this week that the report's findings would be looked at as part of a new investigation by the police's Financial Intelligence Unit.

all_titles.en: Cyprus police open investigation into financial affairs of Roman Abramovich

articles.title_zh: Magnitude-7 earthquake hits Tibet, killing at least 16 and destroying hundreds of homes
facts_zh: Search and rescue efforts under way after quake strikes region’s north, with at least seven aftershocks recorded A magnitude-7 earthquake has hit Tibet, killing at least 16 people, injuring 54 and destroying hundreds of homes in the northern regional city of Nagqu, official media have said.
Search and rescue efforts continued after at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds collapsed, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials.
It was the biggest quake in the region in the past five years, according to China’s national broadcaster CCTV.

articles.title_zh: Powerful earthquake hits Tibet killing 16 people, reports say
facts_zh:
Powerful earthquake hits Tibet killing 16 people, reports say
- Published
A magnitude 7.0 earthquake has hit a mountainous region in Tibet, killing at least 16 people and injuring dozens, according to Chinese state media.
The centre of the quake hit Baqên County in the Nagqu region on Thursday night, Xinhua reported, citing the local emergency management bureau.
The county - located in what China calls the Tibet Autonomous Region after annexing it in the 1950s - is 400km (250 miles) north-east of the region's capital, Lhasa.

articles.title_zh: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC investigation finds
facts_zh:
Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC investigation finds
- Published
A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudanese paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system during their long siege and subsequent takeover of the city in Darfur a year ago.

UN human rights chief Volker Türk called the findings "deeply disturbing", saying multiple attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian infrastructure, including health facilities, were serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes.
The RSF has rejected the BBC's findings.

- Published
Amy Acton, the Democratic candidate for governor of the US state of Ohio, has called an attack ad against her that features her estranged mother "despicable".
Acton commented on the campaign ad from her Republican opponent, Vivek Ramaswamy, on Wednesday, saying: "This is despicable, what he's done".
In the ad Acton's mother, Donna Arthur, says Acton "lied her entire life".

articles.title_zh: Paris extends curfew as Marseille and Lyon ban protests after riots
facts_zh:
Paris extends curfew as Marseille and Lyon ban protests after riots
- Published
Paris is extending a partial curfew restricting movement in parts of the city until Monday, as Marseille and Lyon impose a total ban on protests this weekend.
The Louvre, Orsay and Picasso museums in the French capital will also be closed on Saturday as more demonstrations are expected.

France is still reeling from major disorder at the weekend, when large protests against the high cost of living and school conditions were overshadowed by riots and looting that saw business and historic buildings destroyed.

facts_zh:
Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax
- Published
Meta has agreed to a new deal with chief executive Mark Zuckerberg to prevent him from leaving California over a proposed state tax on billionaires.

The agreement gives Zuckerberg, whose wealth is estimated to exceed $200bn (£149bn), even more shares in Meta to make up for the fraction of his fortune he may lose if the tax wins voter approval in November.
The measure would impose a one-time 5% tax on residents with a net worth of more than $1bn.

'Looksmaxxing' influencer Clavicular pleads not guilty to rape charge
- Published
Clavicular, a social media influencer who promotes the "looksmaxxing" trend of young men maximising their attractiveness, has pleaded not guilty to criminal charges including rape.
The 20-year-old, whose real name is Braden Peters, was charged in September with felony rape, drugging an individual for sexual intercourse and procuring alcohol for someone under the age of 21.
The charges stem from an incident in 2025 when he is accused of assaulting a 17-year-old girl at his family's Massachusetts home.

A foreign national has been beaten to death by a crowd of about 50 people in Durban, South Africa, police say.
According to police, the unidentified man, believed to be in his late 30s or early 40s, was first approached by two men by the roadside before being assaulted by a larger group.
He was pronounced dead at the scene.

articles.title_zh: Newborn twins fight for survival as conflict fuels Yemen's hunger crisis
facts_zh:
Newborn twins fight for survival as conflict fuels Yemen's hunger crisis
- Published
From the day they were born, just seven weeks ago, twins Raghad Hassan and her brother Raad have been battling for survival.
They came into the world prematurely, as fighting surged in Yemen's long-running civil war between Houthi rebel fighters and government forces.

When the Houthis reached their village in the Kahboub mountains in south-west Yemen, their family of seven was forced to flee amid bombs, missiles, and drone attacks – the twins protected only by blankets.

all_titles.en: Newborn twins fight for survival as conflict fuels Yemen's hunger crisis

articles.title_zh: Teacher in Oregon shooting said she pretended to be dead to survive
facts_zh:
Teacher in Oregon shooting said she pretended to be dead to survive
- Published
Some readers may find this article distressing.
A 54-year-old teacher who survived a mass shooting at an Oregon elementary school said she pretended to be dead so the gunman would not shoot her again.
Becky Drury, a teacher at Silver Rail Elementary School, said in a statement shared with US media that as she tried to shut her classroom door, the gunman shot her and she fell to the floor.

all_titles.en: Teacher in Oregon shooting said she pretended to be dead to survive
